related_questions.question: Why do I feel sick after a chiropractic adjustment?

text_blocks.snippet: Feeling sick after a chiropractic adjustment, such as nausea, fatigue, or flu-like symptoms, is often due to the body releasing stored toxins and adjusting to the realignment of the spine. These symptoms are usually temporary and will pass within a day or two as the body adapts to the changes.
snippet_highlighted_words: often due to the body releasing stored toxins and adjusting to the realignment of the spine

list.snippet: Chiropractic adjustments can mobilize toxins that have been stored in the body, particularly around joints.
This release can cause temporary discomfort as the body works to eliminate these toxins.
Symptoms like headache, fatigue, nausea, and even flu-like symptoms can occur as a result.
It's important to note that this is a sign of the body healing and detoxifying, not a cause for alarm.
The spine is interconnected with various systems in the body, and adjustments can cause the body to shift and realign.
This realignment process can temporarily affect muscles, nerves, and even the digestive system.
Fatigue, soreness, or even digestive changes (like increased bowel movements) are common as the body adjusts.
The severity and duration of these side effects vary from person to person.
Most people experience a temporary worsening of symptoms for 24-48 hours.
If symptoms persist for more than a few days, it's best to consult with the chiropractor or another healthcare professional.
Rest: Allow your body time to recover.
Hydration: Drink plenty of water to help flush out toxins.
Gentle Activity: Engage in light exercise or stretching to promote circulation and healing.
Heat or Ice: Apply heat or ice packs to any sore areas.
Communicate with your chiropractor: Discuss any concerns or persistent symptoms.
